main_claim: Past-tense reformulation of harmful requests jailbreaks many SOTA LLMs, exposing a refusal-training generalization gap.
evidence: Ten named LLMs; GPT-4o attack success rises from 1% to 88% on JailbreakBench.
rationale: Question title; abstract claims scoped to tested models with numbers; broader conclusion hedged ('can be brittle', 'not always').

main_claim: CAVs enable quantitative testing of relative concept importance in trained networks without retraining.
evidence: Qualitative demonstrations; CAVs learned from small example sets; no benchmarks or numbers.
rationale: Name-plus-description title; abstract mainly describes capabilities with modest 'we show' claims that do not exceed its demonstrations.

main_claim: Full-batch training with explicit regularization matches SGD performance on CIFAR-10.
evidence: CIFAR-10 with modern architectures only.
rationale: 'Not Necessary for Generalization' reads generally; abstract tests one dataset. Existential claim partly supported by one counterexample, so mild.

main_claim: Linear probes on CoT activations predict final-response safety early, outperforming text-based monitors.
evidence: Average +13 F1 over best alternatives; multiple model sizes, families and safety benchmarks.
rationale: Question/'Towards' title; claims quantified and tested across stated settings; implications hedged ('could enable').

main_claim: Modality-based recommenders with end-to-end training are competitive with, sometimes exceeding, ID-based models.
evidence: Experiments with text and vision modalities across regular, cold and new-item scenarios.
rationale: Question title; abstract hedges ('in some cases', 'imply') and stays within its evidence.

main_claim: Structured (LaTeX) document text induces structured attention and improves MLLM document QA.
evidence: Systematic and attention analyses; no benchmarks, models or numbers named.
rationale: 'Significantly enhance ... across diverse document types' is unquantified; title's attention claim partly backed by attention analysis.

main_claim: Diverse-prompt self-ensembles (DIV-SE, IDIV-SE) improve LLM reasoning accuracy under a fixed generation budget.
evidence: GPT-3.5 and GPT-4 on several reasoning benchmarks; +29.6 points on Blocksworld 4/5.
rationale: Title generalises to LLMs; abstract tests one model family (GPT-3.5/4), matching the codebook's mild example.

main_claim: Instruction tuning on 3D-GRAND significantly improves grounding and reduces hallucination in 3D-LLMs.
evidence: 40,087 scenes, 6.2M instructions; 3D-POPE benchmark; scaling and early sim-to-real signals.
rationale: 'Significantly enhances' unquantified; 'early signals' turned into synthetic-to-real performance and 'critical role' claims.

main_claim: SMPE composes 1D equivariant layers for multi-dimensional equivariance and outperforms state-of-the-art models.
evidence: Auction design, pseudo-inverse, wireless allocation tasks; up to 8.4% and 14.4% gains.
rationale: Named-framework title; outperformance tied to named tasks with numbers.

main_claim: DistillMatch distils VFM features for multimodal image matching and outperforms existing algorithms.
evidence: Experiments on unnamed public datasets; no numbers.
rationale: Descriptive title; one definite but vague comparative claim; absence of numbers alone is not overreach.

main_claim: Learning exogenous distributions improves SCM surrogate fidelity and causal Bayesian optimization.
evidence: Unnamed 'diverse datasets and application scenarios'; no numbers.
rationale: Descriptive title; advantages asserted definitely but vaguely; nothing claimed beyond the stated scope.

main_claim: Detectors degrade severely under image corruptions; stylized training images substantially improve robustness.
evidence: PASCAL-C, COCO-C, Cityscapes-C; performance drops to 30-60% of original.
rationale: Descriptive title; claims tied to named benchmarks with numbers; 'comprehensive' benchmark is not sweeping.

main_claim: GMDP high-dimensional prototypes reduce knowledge shift, outperforming baselines and SOTA in incremental detection.
evidence: PASCAL VOC and MS-COCO; four baselines; no numbers given.
rationale: 'Large margin' and 'significantly outperforms' unquantified; comparative title supported on two standard benchmarks.

main_claim: syre provably removes symmetry-induced low-capacity states; removal correlates with improved optimization.
evidence: Two proven mechanisms; empirical correlation with improvement where entrapment is a concern.
rationale: Title asserts removal improves optimization unconditionally; abstract hedges to correlation under specific conditions.

main_claim: Interventional Dual Attention counters contextual bias, improving classification and detection at lower computation.
evidence: SOTA multi-label classification on MS-COCO and PASCAL-VOC; detection results unspecified.
rationale: Method-name title; SOTA tied to named benchmarks; 'significant improvements' unquantified but within stated scope.

main_claim: Policy-gradient mask learning prunes LLMs structurally without back-propagation and outperforms SOTA pruning.
evidence: LLaMA 1/2/3, Vicuna, Mistral; C4, WikiText2; 2.7h and 35GB for 13B.
rationale: Title slogan describes a method property, not a result; claims scoped to named models, datasets and numbers.

main_claim: DROP's non-iterative bi-level offline RL achieves comparable or better performance than prior methods.
evidence: 'Various benchmarks', unnamed; no numbers.
rationale: Empirical claim modest, but 'fully answered the above three questions' is definitive wording without support.

main_claim: LLMs benefit from graph structure mainly when node text is scarce; homophily, not leakage, tracks performance.
evidence: Node classification with textual features; several prompting methods; rich vs scarce text settings.
rationale: Question title; findings hedged and scoped to node classification.

main_claim: Neural-PSRL makes posterior sampling practical for continuous control and reaches state-of-the-art results.
evidence: SOTA on HalfCheetah-v3 and Hopper-v3 only.
rationale: Title claims to make RL sample efficient generally; abstract reports two MuJoCo domains, mirroring the codebook's clear example.

main_claim: Lambda layers model long-range interactions without attention, outperforming convolutional and attention models efficiently.
evidence: ImageNet, COCO; 3.2-4.4x faster than EfficientNets; 86.7% ImageNet top-1.
rationale: Descriptive name title; strong comparisons backed by named benchmarks and numbers.

main_claim: ASCENSION's GMM-controlled VAE latent expansion improves time-series augmentation and excels on all trilemma aspects.
evidence: UCR archive, 102 datasets; about 7% average accuracy gain.
rationale: 'Excelling in all aspects of the trilemma' lacks reported quality/speed/diversity evidence; title's general trilemma vs time-series-only setting.

main_claim: Chain-of-Causal Reasoning decomposes intents into functional requirements, improving 3D intent grounding and localization.
evidence: Experiments on 3D intention grounding and 3D visual grounding tasks; no numbers.
rationale: Slogan-plus-method title; result claim modest and scoped to named tasks.

main_claim: AdaFGL, adaptive propagation for structure non-IID federated subgraphs, achieves SOTA on five benchmarks.
evidence: Five benchmark datasets under community-split and structure non-IID settings.
rationale: Unqualified 'new paradigm' in title and abstract; 'general federated data settings' broader than the tested settings.

main_claim: Rewarding intra-life novelty (DeepCS) matches SOTA on Montezuma's Revenge and improves other Atari games.
evidence: Montezuma, Amidar, Freeway, Gravitar, Tutankham; doubles A2C on Seaquest.
rationale: Tentative 'Can Improve' title supported on several hard Atari games; conclusion hedged ('suggests').

main_claim: SHARCS shared concept space gives explainable multimodal predictions and improves predictive performance.
evidence: No datasets or numbers; scenarios: missing-modality retrieval, cross-modal explanations.
rationale: 'Significantly outperform' unquantified; 'easily applicable to different types and number of modalities' unsupported by stated evidence.

main_claim: LLMs perform near random at inferring causation from correlation; fine-tuned models fail out of distribution.
evidence: Corr2Cause, 200K+ samples, 17 LLMs; in- vs out-of-distribution perturbations.
rationale: Question title; claims scoped to 17 tested LLMs; 'first benchmark' qualified by 'pure causal inference'.

main_claim: GraphGen handles domain, open-set and source-free shifts jointly and outperforms state-of-the-art methods.
evidence: Unnamed benchmark datasets; no numbers.
rationale: 'Significant improvements' and 'comprehensively address' unquantified; slogan title scoped by its subtitle and broadly matched.

main_claim: DataInf approximates influence accurately and orders of magnitude faster, suited to LoRA fine-tuning.
evidence: RoBERTa-large, Llama-2-13B-chat, stable-diffusion-v1.5; theoretical analysis.
rationale: 'Efficiently' supported by reported speed-ups; claims scoped to named models.

main_claim: An online meta-learned auxiliary actor loss improves off-policy actor-critic learning.
evidence: Continuous control environments with DDPG, TD3 and SAC.
rationale: Descriptive title; result scoped to named base algorithms and environment family.

main_claim: Sage reliably evaluates LLM judges without human labels; top LLM judges are substantially inconsistent.
evidence: 650 questions; correlation with LLMBar and RewardBench2; top models inconsistent in ~25% of hard cases.
rationale: Core claim supported; 'situational preference' explanation and 'fine-tuning is unreliable' stated generally without described evidence.

main_claim: Heavy-tailed gradient noise is a root cause of SGD underperforming Adam on attention models.
evidence: Empirical and theoretical evidence; convergence analysis; ACClip beats Adam on BERT pretraining and finetuning.
rationale: Causal claim backed by stated empirical and theoretical evidence; title's 'Why' only slightly stronger than 'a root cause'.

main_claim: MMTEB provides 500+ embedding tasks over 1,000+ languages; downsampled benchmarks preserve rankings cheaply.
evidence: 500+ tasks, 1,000+ languages; model evaluations; multilingual-e5-large-instruct best public model.
rationale: Name title; 'largest to date' is a countable resource claim backed by numbers (rule 4).

main_claim: Several popular MI objectives can yield representations insufficient for optimal control under mild MDP assumptions.
evidence: Theoretical sufficiency conditions; deep RL experiments on one simulated visual game.
rationale: Question title; theorem-based claims with stated assumptions; hedged 'can yield'.

main_claim: Polylogarithmic width suffices for GD/SGD on two-layer ReLU nets to reach epsilon test error.
evidence: Theorems with stated iteration and sample complexities; positive separation margin of limiting kernel.
rationale: Sufficiency title is strong but backed by a stated theorem without dropping its assumptions (rule 3).

main_claim: Unconstrained-latent models (ViMON, OP3) beat spatial-transformer models; none handle the hardest tracking scenarios.
evidence: Benchmark of three datasets and seven test sets; four methods compared.
rationale: Descriptive title; abstract hedged ('suggest', 'may provide').

main_claim: At equal parameter budgets, CNN ensembles often beat single networks in accuracy and training speed.
evidence: Various architectures and datasets; controlled parameter counts; training time, inference time, memory.
rationale: Exploratory 'When and How' title; finding scoped to 'a wide design space', not stated universally.

main_claim: Negative out-of-distribution augmentation improves GANs, anomaly detection and contrastive representation learning.
evidence: Proof under suitable conditions; image generation, anomaly detection, image/video downstream tasks.
rationale: Topic-name title; claims scoped to listed tasks; broader generalisation hedged ('suggest').

main_claim: One hidden node suffices to reconstruct an input from gradients; batches need width exceeding B.
evidence: Theoretical results; validation on fMRI, ECG, cell images, MNIST, CIFAR100, faces.
rationale: Question title; strong 'enough to reconstruct' backed by stated theory and empirical validation.

main_claim: Augmented GNNs with skip connections and normalization outperform message-passing GNNs on hard hidden-clique instances.
evidence: Synthetic random-graph datasets at varying difficulty.
rationale: 'Learning to solve' read as task description, not a 'Solving Y' claim; results scoped to synthetic hard instances.

main_claim: Task weights change only the scaling-law multiplier; translation direction, not language similarity, matters.
evidence: Large-scale multilingual NMT scaling study; in- and out-of-domain tests; ChrF, BLEURT.
rationale: Predicting performance 'with any language weighting at any scale' extrapolates beyond tested settings.

main_claim: OmniLayout-1M and coarse-to-fine OmniLayout-LLM give strong layout generation, surpassing experts and general LLMs.
evidence: Six document types; multiple domains of the M6Doc dataset; no numbers.
rationale: 'Universal' (codebook level-3 cue) in title vs six document types evaluated on one dataset.

main_claim: Conic Linear Units outperform ReLU across MLP, ResNet, UNet and significantly improve diffusion training.
evidence: Model families named; no datasets or numbers reported.
rationale: 'Significantly', 'wide range', 'fundamentally changes' unquantified; title credits equivariance without isolating it from other design choices.

main_claim: Generative model identification from a single example image achieves over 80% top-4 accuracy.
evidence: Average top-4 identification accuracy above 80% from one image.
rationale: Title promises finding 'the most suitable' model from one image; abstract reports top-4 accuracy around 80%.

main_claim: Hyperbolic sphere-packing feature learning (HACK) yields emergent prototypicality enabling superior instance selection.
evidence: Qualitative observation of images moving toward the origin; no datasets or numbers.
rationale: 'Superior' selection with generalization and robustness benefits asserted without any stated comparison or setting.

main_claim: Good representations alone are insufficient for sample-efficient RL unless approximation quality passes sharp thresholds.
evidence: Lower bounds for value-, model- and policy-based representations; exponential separations.
rationale: Question title; strong statements backed by stated lower bounds (rule 3).

main_claim: G2PTL geography-graph pre-training improves delivery-address encoding for logistics tasks.
evidence: Four downstream logistics tasks on real-world data; production deployment at Cainiao.
rationale: Descriptive title; claims scoped to logistics tasks; 'significantly improves' unquantified but within setting.

main_claim: Meta-SpikeFormer reaches SOTA SNN accuracy and supports classification, detection and segmentation.
evidence: ImageNet-1K 80.0% top-1, +3.7% over SNN SOTA; detection and segmentation results.
rationale: 'Overwhelming performance advantages' exceeds a 3.7% gain; title asserts chip-design inspiration the abstract only discusses.

main_claim: HumorBench shows LLM progress on STEM reasoning transfers effectively to humor comprehension.
evidence: About 300 cartoon-caption pairs; benchmarking of current SOTA models; no numbers.
rationale: Reasoning transfer inferred from correlational benchmarking on ~300 items, stated as 'strong transferability of reasoning abilities'.

main_claim: Adding image reconstruction to pruning helps pruned networks transfer, outperforming SOTA on downstream tasks.
evidence: Unnamed benchmark downstream tasks; no numbers.
rationale: Claim that image-level pretraining 'is not capable' of pruning for diverse tasks stated absolutely without described evidence.

main_claim: Contractive ODE-based graph layers co-evolving features and adjacency improve GNN adversarial robustness.
evidence: Theoretical derivation; numerous real-world benchmarks with on-par or improved performance.
rationale: Title claim within stated setting matches abstract; empirical claim modest ('on par or improved').
